messages.author: ade265a9824fe8a8
messages.subject: Locally-scoped random draws
parts:
Hi there,

I have an application where I am marginalizing over large raggedly-sparse column-stochastic matrices satisfying certain constraints and I am interested in computing statistics using reweighted row sums of these matrices. I am not interested in the entries of these matrices themselves and would like to locally scope the random matrices so that they are discarded after taking the relevant row sums - to save memory. Is there any ways to do this?

Right now I am storing the ragged sparse matrix as a vector in row-sparse format. I want each column to be a realization of a Dirichlet random variable. The way I am doing it right now is drawing a random Gamma random variable vector and then normalizing each column by the column sum. Then I compute the row sums (tau). Any help is greatly appreciated.

transformed parameters{
    vector[tau_df] normalized_allocations;                        // normalize the gamma random variables and rescale to dt
    vector[N_intervals] normalizations;
    vector[N_jobs] tau;                                           // time spent on each job
    normalizations <- rep_vector(0,N_intervals);
    for(jk in 1:tau_df){
        // renormalize for the simplex here  to yield Dirichlet random variables
        normalizations[tau_k[jk]] <- normalizations[tau_k[jk]] + unnormalized_alocations[jk];
    }
    for(jk in 1:tau_df){
        // normalize the time allocated
        normalized_allocations[jk] <- unnormalized_alocations[jk]/normalizations[tau_k[jk]] * interval_lengths[tau_k[jk]]; // tau_k tells us which column the particular entry belongs to
    }
    for (j in 1:N_jobs){
        tau[j] <- sum(normalized_allocations[job_offset[j]:(job_offset[j] + job_alive_num_bins[j]-1) ]); // row sum
    }
}

model {
    lambda ~ uniform(0.05,1000);
    unnormalized_alocations ~ gamma(0.5,1);
    // shape ~ uniform(0.1,2);
    for (j in 1:N_jobs){
        tau[j] ~ weibull(shape[jobstatuscode[j]],lambda[jobstatuscode[j]]);
    }
}

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Locally-scoped random draws
parts:
The only way to do this is to use the same set of random draws that are
consistent over all iterations — otherwise you’d need a pseudo-marginal
method which Stan does not support — in which case you don’t need a
random number generator.
